summary.text:
Erewash carries no external debt. §3.18 (p.4) is verbatim: 'The Council had no borrowing requirement during the year 2025/26 and remains debt free.' Our PWLB price book returns no borrower on any name variant. Both sides tie: nothing to reconcile because there is nothing there. Balance-sheet identity is trivially satisfied — CFR opens and closes at 0 per §3.17, external borrowing 0 per §3.18, closing OLTL implied 0.

The investment side is modest. Average internally managed balance £31.037m at 4.092%; year-end position stated as £23.475m in the text of §3.4 (p.2), with the sector table in the same paragraph adding to £29.919m across the DMO (£21.500m), other local authorities (£8.000m) and a working bank balance (£419k). Two totals in one paragraph that do not reconcile — recorded verbatim, not raiseable; Appendix 1 would resolve it and Appendix 1 is not attached to the covering PDF we hold. Investment interest £1.396m against a £1.200m budget, the variance attributed at §3.7 to rates holding up better than forecast and to Towns Fund capital slippage keeping cash balances higher for longer. Our arithmetic check (£31.037m × 4.092% = £1.270m) is within £126k of what was received, consistent with a peak-above-average balance profile.

Performance sat above SONIA on the 1-month (+42bp), 3-month (+25bp) and 1-year (+32bp) buckets and 17bp below on 7-day (§3.8). Capital expenditure of £9.927m in the year (§3.12) was financed entirely by grants, receipts and reserves — nothing fell to borrowing. §3.11 records compliance with all treasury and prudential indicators; the £-values sit in Appendix 3 which is not attached.

No email drafted. The paper is thin from an outreach angle: debt-free small district, small mostly-DMO investment book, no maturity profile because there is no debt, no LOBOs, no liability benchmark, no MRP policy change, no dated testable assumption in the paper, and no cross-council pattern this paper connects to. The observations we could make (77bp better than 7-day SONIA elsewhere in the curve; £8m out to other local authorities on the lender side of a market some councils are on the wrong side of) would be minor and would risk padding — the pipeline is explicit that padded emails are a fail. The three internal-only quirks (§3.4 unreconciled totals, §3.8 header typo, §3.17 unit ambiguity) are all disclosure issues we would not lead a first contact with. The S151 is unnamed in the paper — the cover styles the author as 'Director of Resources' without naming the postholder, so any first contact would need a separate source anyway. A thin note is the correct outcome here.
